content:
maria: Quick sync—question about private e2e handshake constraints for CP separation. We have two options: 1) customer VPC peering + minimal control plane surface (ephemeral relays) and 2) per-customer private endpoints with the CP in our VPC. Tradeoffs: routing complexity, NAT/SNAT, cert distribution, ops cost, and failover behaviour. Thoughts?

arjun: Short: peering is cheaper at scale but increases blast radius and route-table churn. Private endpoints simplify firewalling for customers but blow up our endpoint fleet and per-region infra. Also peering complicates cross-account route policy and sharing.

sam: +1 on route-table churn. Also: peering makes it hard to preserve source IP for egress flows. If a customer requires source IP preservation we either need to honor it via an SNAT workaround or force private endpoints.

jen: Onboarding time matters. Large customers frequently require manual peering approvals or legal/security signoffs—this can add hours/days. Private endpoints can often be provisioned faster from our side (but they need per-tenant infra).

maria: Good. Cert rotation question: with peering we can terminate mTLS in the CP and keep certs centralized; with private endpoints we need a secure, auditable way to distribute and rotate endpoint certs inside customer infra. ops-bot: (system) cert rotation policy reminder — rotation due in 2 weeks :calendar:

arjun: Implementation idea: hybrid default. Use peering+relay overlay for low-SLA customers; use private endpoints for customers that need egress IP preservation, strict firewalling, or faster isolation. Relay would be ephemeral agents in customer subnets with a tight controlplane handshake. Sketch: 
``
relay: {
  mode: ephemeral-hostnetwork,
  nat: true,
  control_channel: privatelink,
  cert: signed-by-our-ca-or-customer-ca?
}
```
This lets us reduce per-endpoint infra while still giving isolation when needed.

kevin: Big concern: ephemeral hostNetwork relays require cross-account roles/instance profiles + least-privilege IAM. That increases ops complexity and makes autoscaling trickier. We'd need a secure bootstrap token flow and revocation.

sam: Ops counters: central operator manages relay lifecycle, rotates relays every X hours, and keeps an observability sidecar back to the Console over Privatelink for health and logs. DNS split is another tricky surface—customers expect internal names to resolve to internal endpoints and not leak.

maria: Right—DNS split and zone forwarding are must-haves. We should ensure the relay doesn't accidentally forward internal DNS to the public internet. Also consider failure modes: if relays die, traffic should fail open to a lower-capacity fallback model or to a queued state.

jen: Actionable spike: I'll prototype relay bootstrap + token revocation flow and test cross-account IAM patterns. I'll validate autoscale and cert injection. ETA: EOW.

arjun: I'll draft a short decision matrix (peering vs endpoint vs hybrid) with cost curves and failure diagrams, include egress IP preservation implications for sales/security.

kevin: I'll run a rough TCO for per-endpoint infra in 3 regions and share numbers. Also will surface IAM changes required.

infra-bot: deployment started for branch relay-spike #1234 — running tests :rocket:

maria: Thanks all — unless there are objections I'll mark this as the follow-up plan and create a tracker ticket linking the spike, TCO, and matrix. :thumbsup:

arjun: No objections from me.

sam: LGTM

jen: noted, will post updates in this thread.
